chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, who said:
I said to him: If a man performs zihar in Sha'ban and does not find what he can free, he said:
He should wait until he fasts the month of Ramadan, then he should fast
If he performs zihar while he is traveling, he should wait until he returns. And if he fasts and then acquires wealth, then he should continue with what he had begun.

key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: the month of Sha'ban, mentioned as the time when zihar occurred
key_terms.شَهْرَ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, whose fasting affects the timing of the expiation
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months, the required fasting expiation in this case
key_terms.ظَاهَرَ: performed zihar, declaring his wife unlawful by likening her to a prohibited relative
key_terms.مَالًا: wealth or property, referring to later financial ability
key_terms.مُسَافِرٌ: a traveler, whose state delays the commencement of the ruling
key_terms.يُعْتِقُ: to free a slave, the first form of expiation referred to here

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the expiation of zihar if a man cannot afford to free a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the expiation of zihar when a person cannot free a slave. It states that if the declaration occurs in Sha'ban, he should wait until after fasting Ramadan and then fast two consecutive months, and if he begins the fasting expiation and later becomes financially able, he should continue the expiation he already started.
